components.text: The first digit of the three-digit code tells you the class of outcome. The other two narrow it down.
**Rule of thumb:** a 4xx will fail again until you change the request. A 5xx may succeed if you retry later.

classes.name: Informational
classes.meaning: Request received, keep going. These are interim responses.

codes.name: Continue
codes.desc: Headers received; the client may send the body.

codes.name: Switching Protocols
codes.desc: The connection is being upgraded, for example to WebSocket.

classes.name: Success
classes.meaning: The request was received, understood and accepted.

codes.name: OK
codes.desc: The standard success response, with a body.

codes.name: Created
codes.desc: A new resource was created, typically after POST.

codes.name: No Content
codes.desc: Success with nothing to return, common for DELETE.

classes.name: Redirection
classes.meaning: The client must look somewhere else to finish the request.

codes.name: Moved Permanently
codes.desc: The resource has a new permanent URL; update links.

codes.name: Found
codes.desc: Temporary redirect; keep using the original URL.

codes.name: Not Modified
codes.desc: The cached copy is still valid; no body is sent.

classes.name: Client error
classes.meaning: The request itself is wrong. Fix it before retrying.

codes.name: Unauthorized
codes.desc: Not authenticated; log in or send credentials.

codes.name: Too Many Requests
codes.desc: Rate limited; slow down and retry later.

classes.name: Server error
classes.meaning: The server failed to fulfil a valid request.

codes.name: Internal Server Error
codes.desc: An unhandled failure on the server.

codes.name: Bad Gateway
codes.desc: A proxy got an invalid response from upstream.

codes.name: Service Unavailable
codes.desc: Overloaded or down for maintenance; usually temporary.

codes.name: Gateway Timeout
codes.desc: A proxy gave up waiting for upstream.
